_about: THE LOW STARTS (LOW START DESIGN, stage 2): life below the chair in the Valente family. Orders that come down from your capo or the Don (followups the engine schedules every few weeks, valente.ts ORDER_SCENES), and the pressures of a man who is nobody yet: the other kid who wants your slot, the made man you cannot touch, the Don's son, the arrest, the offer from another family. Every scene names its ranks (when.station). Written 2026-11-03.

scenes.title: {capo.first} wants his money back
scenes.text: {capo.call} slides a slip of paper across the booth: a name, an address on Spencer Avenue, a number. "Owes me nine hundred since Easter. Owns a dry cleaner's, so don't tell me he don't have it. Bring it back by Saturday. All of it."

choices.label: Go see him. Be polite the first time
choices.hint: Patience usually works on a man with a shop and a family.
choices.result: The cleaner paid, in an envelope, with an apology. {capo.first} counted it and nodded.
choices.failText: The cleaner cried, and you came back with three hundred and a story. {capo.first} did not want the story.

choices.label: Go see him with a tire iron in the car
choices.hint: Faster. Louder. People talk.
choices.result: He paid before you got the trunk open. The whole block saw you leave.
choices.failText: His brother-in-law is a county detective. Now there is a report with your description on it.

choices.label: Pay {capo.first} the nine hundred yourself and let the man owe you
choices.hint: The money is gone, but now a man on Spencer Avenue owes you, not him.
choices.result: {capo.first} took your money and looked at you a long time. "Smart," he said, and you could not tell if he meant it.

scenes.title: Hold this for me
scenes.text: {capo.call} hands you a paper bag from the Acme, folded over twice, heavy for its size. "Keep it at your mother's. Don't open it. I'll want it back in a week." He doesn't say what's in it. He doesn't have to say that he knows exactly how much it is.

choices.label: Count it, then put it away
choices.hint: So you know. He might know you know.

opinion.why: The folds on the bag were wrong

choices.result: Six thousand two hundred. You folded it back the same way. He never said a word.
choices.failText: He looked at the folds on the bag and then at you. "Somebody's curious."

choices.label: Skim fifty. He'll never miss it
choices.hint: He will.
choices.result: He didn't miss it. This time.
choices.failText: He counted it in front of you and said the number out loud, fifty short. Then he hit you once, very hard, and said you were lucky it was him.

choices.label: Put it in your mother's cellar and don't look
choices.hint: This is a test. Most tests are this simple.

opinion.why: Held the bag and never looked

choices.result: A week later he weighed the bag in his hand, opened it in front of you and counted it. Then he gave you two hundred out of it.
choices.failText: Your cousin found it in the cellar. Forty dollars gone. {capo.first} believes it wasn't you, almost.

scenes.title: Something ugly
scenes.text: {capo.call} doesn't look at you while he says it. A bartender at the Riptide has been telling people things about the family, things a bartender hears. "I want him in the hospital, not the paper. Tonight. You and whoever you trust."

choices.label: Do it. Exactly what he asked, nothing more
choices.hint: This is how men get noticed.

opinion.why: Did the ugly thing and kept quiet

choices.result: The bartender went to Burdette Tomlin with two broken ribs and told the nurses he fell. {capo.first} bought you a drink, which he has never done.
choices.failText: It got done, but a cab driver saw your face under the streetlight. The police have a description.

choices.label: Tell {capo.first} you won't do it
choices.hint: A man can say no once. Maybe.
choices.result: {capo.first} looked at you like he was writing something down. Somebody else went to the Riptide that night.

choices.label: Talk to the bartender first. Scare him without a mark
choices.hint: Cleaner. Not what you were told.

opinion.why: Did it his own way, and it didn't work

choices.result: The bartender quit Monday and moved to his sister's in Camden. {capo.first} said, "Fine," in a voice that meant it would have to be.
choices.failText: The bartender laughed at you and kept talking. Now {capo.first} has to send somebody else, and everybody knows why.

scenes.title: Sit on him
scenes.text: "I want to know where {mark.call} goes at night," {capo.first} says. "Who he eats with. A week." {mark.first} is one of ours. You understand what it means that somebody wants to know.

choices.label: Watch him, and leave out the part that would hurt him
choices.hint: A friend now, or the truth for your capo.

opinion.why: Covered for me and never said

choices.result: You told {capo.first} {mark.first} goes home to his wife. Almost true.

choices.label: Warn {mark.first}
choices.hint: If {capo.first} ever finds out, you are done.

opinion.why: Warned the man I was watching

choices.result: {mark.first} owes you his life, maybe. He knows it.
choices.failText: {mark.first} told somebody who told {capo.first}.

choices.label: Watch him, and bring back everything

opinion.why: Followed me around for a week

choices.result: {mark.first} has dinner twice a week with a man from Kessler's crew. You told {capo.first}. You do not know what happens next, and you don't ask.
choices.failText: {mark.first} made you on the second night. He waved.

scenes.title: A truck off Route 47
scenes.text: {capo.call} has a tip: a load of Zenith television sets coming through Rio Grande on Thursday, a driver who will stop for coffee and take a long time over it. "The family gets half," he says. "You get the rest to split with your guys. Don't make it messy."

choices.label: Take it, and send the family's half up the same night

opinion.why: The half came up the same night

choices.result: Forty televisions in a garage in Cold Spring by midnight. The family's half went up before you slept.
choices.failText: The driver lost his nerve and called the state police. You got away with nothing but a federal problem.

choices.label: Take it, and keep a little more than your half
choices.hint: Everybody shaves. Nobody admits it.
choices.result: Nobody counted the televisions but you.
choices.failText: The fence told {capo.first} how many sets there were. {capo.first} can count.

choices.label: Pass. Federal is federal
choices.result: {capo.first} gave it to somebody else. The somebody else is doing well this month.

scenes.title: Downtown by Labor Day
scenes.text: The word comes down through {capo.call}: the Don wants more of Downtown before the season ends. Not a war. More bars paying, more slips on Pacific. "He said your name," {capo.first} says. "Don't make him say it twice."

choices.label: Do it the slow way: buy drinks, make friends
choices.hint: Less heat, less to show.
choices.result: Four bars, no trouble. Not what he asked for, but nobody got hurt and nobody got arrested.

choices.label: Tell {capo.first} it can't be done this summer
choices.result: {capo.first} carried that answer upstairs. He did not come back down smiling.

choices.label: Put your whole crew on it

crew.why: Worked us to the bone for nothing

choices.result: By the end of August eleven more bars on Pacific were paying. The Don sent a bottle of anisette with no note.
choices.failText: Kessler's people pushed back and the bars went quiet. The Don did not send anything.

scenes.title: Stay out of the Crest
scenes.text: One of your soldiers has a card game going in a motel in the Crest. The Crest is {other.call}'s. {capo.call} says the Don has heard about it, which means {other.first} went upstairs instead of coming to you.

choices.label: Go to {other.first} and split the game with him
choices.hint: Capos make deals. Sometimes the Don likes that.

opinion.why: Came to me like a man
Wants a piece of my Crest

choices.result: Half a game is better than none. {other.first} shook on it.
choices.failText: {other.first} told the Don you tried to buy your way into his district.

choices.label: Keep the game open. It's a motel, not a district

opinion.why: Kept a game in my Crest

choices.result: The game stayed open. So did the question of what the Don will do about it.

choices.label: Shut the game and send {other.first} a case of Scotch

opinion.why: Shut his game when I asked

choices.result: The game closed Sunday. {other.first} drank your Scotch and told people you were all right.

scenes.title: Whose idea it was
scenes.text: The jukebox route on Rio Grande Avenue was your idea. You found the bar owners, you found the machines. Last night at the Shamrock, {kid.call} told {capo.first} all about his idea for a jukebox route on Rio Grande Avenue. {capo.first} liked it.

choices.label: Go to {capo.first} with the names and the numbers
choices.hint: Proof. Nobody likes a kid who keeps receipts, but they believe him.

opinion.why: Showed me up in front of the capo

choices.result: {capo.first} read your list twice and put it in his pocket. {kid.first} won't look at you now.
choices.failText: "Who cares whose idea," {capo.first} said. "Bring me money, not paper."

choices.label: Find {kid.first} behind the Shamrock and settle it
choices.hint: He isn't made either. Yet.
choices.result: {kid.first} told {capo.first} the next morning that the route was your idea after all.
choices.failText: He was bigger than he looked. The whole bar heard about it.

choices.label: Let him have it. There will be other ideas

memory.text: He let me take the jukebox route and said nothing

choices.result: {kid.first} got the credit. You got the lesson.

scenes.title: A friend of ours
scenes.text: {made.call} is drunk at the Admiral and wants your stool, so he takes it. Then he takes your cigarettes. Then he says something about your wife to the whole counter. He is a made man. You are not. Everybody at the counter knows exactly what that means.

choices.label: Go to your capo about it
choices.hint: The right way. It costs you a favor.

opinion.why: Went to his capo about me

choices.result: A word was said, somewhere upstairs. {made.first} nodded to you the next time, which is as close to sorry as he gets.
choices.failText: Your capo said a made man is a made man. Learn it.

choices.label: Put him on the floor
choices.hint: You do not hit a made man. Not ever. Not without permission.

opinion.why: An associate put his hands on me

choices.result: It felt good for about an hour. Then the phone rang at your mother's house, and nobody spoke when she answered.

choices.label: Take it. Smile. Leave
choices.hint: The rules are the rules. They will notice that you know them.
choices.result: You paid for his coffee on the way out. Two men at the counter told the story both ways.

scenes.title: The Don's son
scenes.text: {son.call} owes a bookmaker in Atlantic City four thousand dollars and has been telling him to collect from his father. Now the bookmaker is asking around, and somebody pointed him at you. {son.first} catches you outside the Shamrock: "Square it for me. My old man never has to know."

choices.label: Square it quietly, out of your own money
choices.hint: The son owes you. The father may find out anyway.

opinion.why: Squared my book and kept quiet

choices.result: The bookmaker went home happy. {son.first} calls you "pal" now.
choices.failText: The Don found out, the way he finds out everything. He didn't thank you, exactly. But he knows your name now.

choices.label: Tell the Don
choices.hint: Honest. His son will never forgive it.

opinion.why: Told me the truth about my boy

choices.result: The Don paid the bookmaker and slapped his son in front of the waiters at the Bolero. {son.first} will remember who told.

choices.label: Tell {son.first} it isn't your business
choices.result: {son.first} found somebody else. Somebody always helps the Don's son.

scenes.title: Picked up
scenes.text: Two county detectives pick you up outside the cigar store and drive you around for three hours. They know about the slips. They know about {capo.first}. They say they'll forget all of it if you remember a few things about him.

choices.label: Give them something small about somebody else
choices.hint: Nobody ever gives them something small.
choices.result: They let you go. Nobody knows. You will think about it every time a car slows down.
choices.failText: The detective has a cousin who drinks at the Shamrock. By Friday everybody knew.

choices.label: Ask for a lawyer and keep asking
choices.result: A lawyer from Cape May Court House got you out in an hour. {capo.first} paid him back, and wrote it down.

choices.label: Say nothing. Not one word, for three hours
choices.hint: This is the thing they will ask about you when the books open.
choices.result: They let you out on Rio Grande Avenue at two in the morning. By breakfast {capo.first} knew you stood up.
choices.failText: You said nothing, but they kept you overnight and wrote a report anyway. {capo.first} heard the part that matters.

scenes.title: What you do all night
scenes.text: {wife.first} is awake at the kitchen table when you get in at four. "Your mother asked me what you do. I didn't know what to tell her. So you tell me."

choices.label: Tell her the truth. Some of it

opinion.why: Told me the truth, or some of it

choices.result: {wife.first} listened to all of it and then went to bed without a word. In the morning she made your eggs the way you like them.

choices.label: "I work for a man who has a lot of businesses."
choices.result: {wife.first} said that's what her father used to say, and turned out the light.

choices.label: Put two hundred dollars on the table
choices.result: She took it. She didn't stop asking.

scenes.title: An offer from Atlantic City
scenes.text: {rival.call} buys you a drink at the Riptide and doesn't waste time. His people would make you in a year, maybe less. You'd have your own corner. "{capo.first} keeps you running slips because it suits him," he says. "Think about who's going to stand up for you over there."

choices.label: Tell {capo.first} about the offer
choices.hint: Loyalty, said out loud.

opinion.why: Told me when the other side came calling

choices.result: {capo.first} listened, nodded, and said your name to the right people that week.

choices.label: Keep it to yourself and keep the door open
choices.result: You didn't say yes. You didn't say no. In this town that is also an answer.

choices.label: Throw the drink in his face

opinion.why: Threw a drink in my face

choices.result: The whole Riptide saw it. {capo.first} pretended to be angry about it and bought you lunch.

scenes.title: Somebody to stand up for you
scenes.text: {made.call} has been watching you for a while. Over coffee at the Doo Wop he says it plainly: when the books open, somebody has to put his name on you. "I'd do it," he says. "But a man doesn't put his name on a stranger. I need something done first." His brother-in-law is behind on a loan to a Kessler shylock, and the shylock has started making threats.

choices.label: Go see the shylock and make it go away
choices.result: The shylock tore up the paper. {made.first} told you, without being asked, that he'll stand for you.
choices.failText: The shylock called Kessler. Now it is a bigger problem, and it has your name on it.

choices.label: Pay the brother-in-law's debt yourself ($1,500)
choices.result: {made.first} took the money for his brother-in-law and gave you his word. Bought, maybe. Still his word.

choices.label: "I'll earn it some other way."
choices.result: {made.first} shrugged. The offer may come again. It may not.

scenes.title: Light envelopes
scenes.text: You do the arithmetic twice. What your crew brings {capo.first} and what {capo.first} sends upstairs to {ub.call} don't match, and haven't for a month. Someone is going to notice. It might be better if it was you.

choices.label: Tell {ub.first}
choices.hint: Over your capo's head. It can make you, or bury you.

opinion.why: Brought me the truth about his capo

choices.result: {ub.first} looked at your numbers and said nothing. A week later {capo.first}'s envelopes were right again, and {ub.first} knew your name.
choices.failText: {ub.first} told {capo.first} who had been counting. Now you work for a man who knows.

choices.label: Tell {capo.first} that you noticed
choices.hint: Quietly. He'll owe you, or he'll hate you.
choices.result: {capo.first} said it was a misunderstanding and gave you a bigger piece of the next score.
choices.failText: {capo.first} said you must be mistaken, in the voice that means you'd better be.

choices.label: Say nothing. It's not your envelope
choices.result: You kept your mouth shut. That is a skill too.

scenes.title: The underboss wants your vote
scenes.text: {ub.call} takes you for a drive along the bay. The Don is getting older, he says, and when the time comes the capos will have a say. "I'd like to know where you'll stand. I don't forget who stood where."

choices.label: "With you, when the time comes."
choices.result: {ub.first} dropped you at the Shamrock and shook your hand for a long time.

choices.label: Tell the Don about the drive
choices.hint: The Don will remember. So will {ub.first}.

opinion.why: Told me who is counting my days
Ran to the Don about our drive

choices.result: The Don thanked you with a look. {ub.first} has been very polite to you since.
choices.failText: The Don already knew. He wanted to see who would tell him, and how fast. {ub.first} found out who did.

choices.label: "With the Don. While he's alive, there's no time to come."
choices.result: {ub.first} laughed, but not much. Somehow, the Don heard what you said.
